heading: INT. HOSPITAL SUBBASEMENT - LAUNDRY ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HOSPITAL SUBBASEMENT - LAUNDRY ROOM - NIGHT
A low, steam-choked cavern.
Industrial washers thump like slow drums.
Sheet-laden carts line the walls in ghostly rows.
Pipes sweat overhead, and the tiled floor is slick with soap and condensation.
A single fluorescent tube buzzes.
DR. EZEKIEL FAIRWEATHER, 50s, a cardiothoracic surgeon, sits on an overturned laundry bin in rumpled blue scrubs, his tie shoved in his pocket.
Grey stubble.
Hands folded between his knees as if praying.
He has not slept in thirty hours.
He stares at the drain in the floor.
The doors at the far end swing open and a gurney wheel squeals.
PADDY GALLAGHER, 50s, the night porter, pushes a cart of towels down the aisle.
Barrel-chested, flushed, a green cap pulled over a bald crown.
He stops short at the sight of the doctor.
Jesus, Mary and Joseph. Doctor?
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Don't mind me.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: You scared the life out of me.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Sorry.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: It's the wrong end of the building for you, sir. The surgeons have their own lounge.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: I know.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Then why--
units.name: PADDY

units.text: It's loud here.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Paddy considers this.
He parks the cart.
Pulls a crumpled pack of cigarettes from his pocket, glances up at the smoke detector, and puts them back.
Bad one?
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Seven hours. We lost him on the table.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: I'm sorry.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: He was thirty-one.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Ah, God.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: He had a daughter. She was in the waiting room, drawing a horse.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Did you tell her?
units.name: PADDY

units.text: His wife did. I just stood there.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: A washer ends its cycle with a shuddering groan.
Steam breathes out of the vents.
Paddy drags a second bin across the tile and lowers himself onto it with a grunt, so the two men sit knee to knee in the damp.
My brother went the same way. Heart.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: When?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Twenty years. The doctors were very kind.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: That doesn't help, does it?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Not on the day.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: PADDY What does, then? Time, I suppose.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: They both stop.
The ghost of a smile crosses Paddy's face.
Ezekiel laughs, one dry exhale through his nose, and rubs his eyes with the heels of his hands.
You want a towel? They're warm.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: I'm not crying.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Never said you were. They're just warm.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: He passes a folded towel from the cart.
Ezekiel takes it, presses it to his face, and holds it there much longer than a person needs to wipe off sweat.
Paddy gazes politely at a washer.
Time passes in the slow rhythm of the drums.
Thank you.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Aye.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Does it ever stop? The... carrying it?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: I wouldn't know, Doctor. I only carry the linen.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Then you're luckier than I am.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Maybe. Or I just do the washing so you can do the rest.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Ezekiel looks at him properly for the first time.
Paddy meets the look without flinching, wide-faced and unhurried.
What's your name?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Paddy. Paddy Gallagher.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Ezekiel.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: I know. It's on the plaque in the lobby. The one with the donors.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: I never donated.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Your name's on it anyway.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: The ghost of a smile returns.
Ezekiel stands.
He folds the towel into a perfect square and sets it back on the cart, then stands for a moment with his hand on the metal rail.
I should go up.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: They'll keep.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Not all of them.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: No. Not all.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Ezekiel nods.
He straightens his scrubs, pulls his tie from his pocket, and puts it back again.
At the door he pauses.
Paddy.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Doctor.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: Thank you for the towel.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Anytime. It's what I'm for.
units.name: PADDY

units.text: The door sighs shut behind the surgeon.
Paddy sits alone in the thrum of the machines.
After a moment he takes out the cigarettes, looks at the smoke detector again, and slowly, decidedly, puts them back.
